events.text: The “recertify on a swallowed cover” route would need a new finite-support affine-neighborhood theorem and transfer of certificate data, so it is not the cheapest immediate bridge. The existing arbitrary-cover definitions instead expose the canonical descent object: `IntrinsicThetaGluedOver` is a module over the glued divisor algebra, locally invertible on every affine piece. I’m checking whether the project’s descent library can turn those local invertible modules into the missing global projective/rank facts without adding any binder.

    14	/-!
    15	# Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules
    16	
    17	Let `A → B` be a faithfully flat map of commutative rings.  This file shows that the
    18	module-theoretic properties *finite*, *finitely presented*, *flat*, *projective* and
    19	*invertible* all descend along `A → B`: if `B ⊗[A] P` has the property over `B`, then `P`
    20	has it over `A`.  Combined with the effectivity theorem of
    21	`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent` this yields: a `B`-module `M` with a descent
    22	datum descends to an `A`-module `M₀` (unique up to canonical isomorphism), and if `M` is
    23	invertible then so is `M₀`.
    24	
    25	The descent of invertibility is reduced, via the definition
    26	`Module.Invertible R M ↔ Function.Bijective (contractLeft R M)`, to two ingredients:
    27	
    28	* the *dual base-change comparison* `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is an
    29	  isomorphism for `P` finite projective (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`, proved by a
    30	  retract argument from the finite free case, which is `IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight`);
    31	* bijectivity of `A`-linear maps descends along faithfully flat maps
    32	  (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective`).
    33	
    34	Finiteness and projectivity of `P` are themselves obtained by descent: mathlib provides
    35	finiteness (`Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`) and flatness
    36	(`Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`); we add finite presentation
    37	(`Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`), and
    38	projectivity follows from flat + finitely presented.
    39	
    40	## Main declarations
    41	
    42	* `Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`:
    43	  finite presentation descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
    44	* `Module.Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: finite projectivity
    45	  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
    46	* `Module.dualBaseChange A B P : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)`: the dual
    47	  base-change comparison map.
    48	* `Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`: the comparison map is bijective for finite projective
    49	  `P` (over an arbitrary `A`-algebra `B`).
    50	* `Module.Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: invertibility
    51	  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
    52	* `Module.DescentDatum.finite_descended`, `…flat_descended`,
    53	  `…finitePresentation_descended`, `…projective_descended`,
    54	  `…invertible_descended`: for a descent datum on a `B`-module `M` relative to a
    55	  faithfully flat `A → B`, the descended module inherits each property from `M`;
    56	  in particular **an invertible module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
    57	  module**.
    58	
    59	All modules live in a single universe `u`.
    60	-/
    61	
    62	universe u
    63	
    64	open TensorProduct
    65	
    66	namespace Module

    68	variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]

    70	/-! ### Descent of finite presentation -/
    71	
    72	/-- Finite presentation of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
    73	theorem FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
    74	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
    75	    [Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
    76	    Module.FinitePresentation A P := by
    77	  have hfin : Module.Finite A P :=
    78	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
    79	  obtain ⟨n, p, hp⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
    80	  have hpB : Function.Surjective (p.baseChange B) := by
    81	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    82	    exact LinearMap.lTensor_surjective B hp
    83	  have hker : (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)).FG :=
    84	    Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker (p.baseChange B) hpB
    85	  have hexact := Module.Flat.lTensor_exact B p.exact_subtype_ker_map
    86	  have hinj : Function.Injective ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B) := by
    87	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    88	    exact Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _
    89	      (LinearMap.ker p).injective_subtype
    90	  have hrange : LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B)
    91	      = LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) := by
    92	    ext x
    93	    rw [LinearMap.mem_range, LinearMap.mem_ker]
    94	    constructor
    95	    · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩
    96	      simp only [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    97	      exact hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero y
    98	    · intro hx
    99	      rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor] at hx
   100	      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hexact x).mp hx
   101	      exact ⟨y, by rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]; exact hy⟩
   102	  have e : (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) ≃ₗ[B] LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) :=
   103	    (LinearEquiv.ofInjective _ hinj).trans (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ hrange)
   104	  have : Module.Finite B (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)) := Module.Finite.iff_fg.mpr hker
   105	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) := Module.Finite.equiv e.symm
   106	  have : Module.Finite A (LinearMap.ker p) :=
   107	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
   108	  exact Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective p hp (Module.Finite.iff_fg.mp this)
   109	
   110	/-- Finite projectivity of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
   111	theorem Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
   112	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
   113	    [Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] P)] [Projective B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
   114	    Projective A P := by
   115	  have : Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
   116	    Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B (B ⊗[A] P)
   117	  have : Module.FinitePresentation A P :=
   118	    FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B P
   119	  have : Module.Flat A P := Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct A P B
   120	  exact Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation (R := A) (M := P)

   122	/-! ### The dual base-change comparison map -/
   123	
   124	section DualBaseChange
   125	
   126	variable {A B} in
   127	/-- Two `B`-functionals on `B ⊗[A] X` that agree on the tensors `1 ⊗ₜ x` are equal. -/
   128	private theorem dual_ext {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module A X]
   129	    {F G : Dual B (B ⊗[A] X)} (h : ∀ x : X, F (1 ⊗ₜ x) = G (1 ⊗ₜ x)) : F = G := by
   130	  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   131	  apply TensorProduct.ext'
   132	  intro b x
   133	  have hb : b ⊗ₜ[A] x = b • (1 ⊗ₜ[A] x : B ⊗[A] X) := by
   134	    rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
   135	  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, hb, map_smul, h]
   136	
   137	variable (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]
   138	
   139	/-- The canonical `B`-linear comparison map from the base change of the dual to the dual
   140	of the base change, `b ⊗ₜ f ↦ b • (f.baseChange B)`.  It is bijective for finite
   141	projective `P` (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`). -/
   142	noncomputable def dualBaseChange : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
   143	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B (Module.Dual.baseChange B)
   144	
   145	@[simp] theorem dualBaseChange_tmul (b : B) (f : Dual A P) :
   146	    dualBaseChange A B P (b ⊗ₜ f) = b • Module.Dual.baseChange B f := rfl
   147	
   148	/-- Naturality of the dual base-change comparison map. -/
   149	theorem dualBaseChange_naturality {P Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]
   150	    [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q] (g : P →ₗ[A] Q) :
   151	    dualBaseChange A B P ∘ₗ g.dualMap.baseChange B =
   152	      (g.baseChange B).dualMap ∘ₗ dualBaseChange A B Q := by
   153	  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   154	  apply TensorProduct.ext'
   155	  intro b f
   156	  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply]
   157	  refine dual_ext fun x => ?_
   158	  simp [Module.Dual.baseChange_apply_tmul]
   159	
   160	variable {A B} in
   161	private theorem bijective_dualBaseChange_free (n : ℕ) :
   162	    Function.Bijective (dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A)) := by
   163	  have j : IsBaseChange B (TensorProduct.mk A B (Fin n → A) 1) :=
   164	    TensorProduct.isBaseChange A (Fin n → A) B
   165	  have k : IsBaseChange B (Algebra.linearMap A B) := IsBaseChange.linearMap A B
   166	  have hlr : IsBaseChange B (IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom j (Algebra.linearMap A B)) :=
   167	    IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight j k
   168	  have heq : Module.Dual.baseChange (R := A) B (V := Fin n → A)
   169	      = IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom j (Algebra.linearMap A B) := by
   170	    refine LinearMap.ext fun f => dual_ext fun x => ?_
   171	    have h1 := IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom_comp_apply j (Algebra.linearMap A B) f x
   172	    simpa [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one] using h1.symm
   173	  have hlift : dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) = hlr.equiv.toLinearMap := by
   174	    apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   175	    apply TensorProduct.ext'
   176	    intro b f
   177	    simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, dualBaseChange_tmul,
   178	      IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul, heq]
   179	  rw [hlift]
   180	  exact hlr.equiv.bijective
   181	
   182	/-- **The dual commutes with base change for finite projective modules**: the comparison
   183	map `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is bijective when `P` is finite projective. -/
   184	theorem bijective_dualBaseChange [Module.Finite A P] [Projective A P] :
   185	    Function.Bijective (dualBaseChange A B P) := by
   186	  obtain ⟨n, r, hr⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
   187	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := Module.projective_lifting_property r LinearMap.id hr
   188	  have hfree := bijective_dualBaseChange_free (A := A) (B := B) n
   189	  have hnat_r := dualBaseChange_naturality A B r
   190	  have hnat_s := dualBaseChange_naturality A B s
   191	  -- the two retraction identities
   192	  have hcomp : s.dualMap ∘ₗ r.dualMap = LinearMap.id := by
   193	    ext f x
   194	    simpa using congrArg f (LinearMap.congr_fun hs x)
   195	  have hu : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] Dual A P,
   196	      s.dualMap.baseChange B (r.dualMap.baseChange B x) = x := by
   197	    intro x
   198	    rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hcomp, LinearMap.baseChange_id,
   199	      LinearMap.id_apply]
   200	  have hcompB : (r.baseChange B) ∘ₗ (s.baseChange B) = LinearMap.id := by
   201	    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hs, LinearMap.baseChange_id]
   202	  have hv : ∀ y : Dual B (B ⊗[A] P),
   203	      (s.baseChange B).dualMap ((r.baseChange B).dualMap y) = y := by
   204	    intro y
   205	    rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.dualMap_comp_dualMap, hcompB, LinearMap.dualMap_id,
   206	      LinearMap.id_apply]
   207	  constructor
   208	  · intro x y hxy
   209	    have h1 : dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) (r.dualMap.baseChange B x)
   210	        = dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) (r.dualMap.baseChange B y) := by
   211	      rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, hnat_r, ← LinearMap.comp_apply, hnat_r]
   212	      simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, hxy]
   213	    have h2 := hfree.injective h1
   214	    rw [← hu x, ← hu y, h2]
   215	  · intro y
   216	    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hfree.surjective ((r.baseChange B).dualMap y)
   217	    refine ⟨s.dualMap.baseChange B z, ?_⟩
   218	    have := LinearMap.congr_fun hnat_s z
   219	    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply] at this
   220	    rw [this, hz, hv]
   221	
   222	end DualBaseChange

   224	/-! ### Descent of invertibility -/
   225	
   226	/-- **Invertibility of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps**: if `A → B` is
   227	faithfully flat and `B ⊗[A] P` is an invertible `B`-module, then `P` is an invertible
   228	`A`-module. -/
   229	theorem Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
   230	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
   231	    [Module.Invertible B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
   232	    Module.Invertible A P := by
   233	  have hfin : Module.Finite A P :=
   234	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
   235	  have hproj : Projective A P :=
   236	    Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B P
   237	  -- the contraction square: base change of `contractLeft A P` factors through
   238	  -- `contractLeft B (B ⊗[A] P)` via the dual base-change comparison map
   239	  have hsquare : (contractLeft A P).baseChange B =
   240	      ((AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ contractLeft B (B ⊗[A] P) ∘ₗ
   241	          (dualBaseChange A B P).rTensor (B ⊗[A] P)) ∘ₗ
   242	        (AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange A B (Dual A P) P).toLinearMap := by
   243	    apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   244	    ext f p
   245	    simp only [AlgebraTensorModule.curry_apply, LinearMap.restrictScalars_self, curry_apply,
   246	      LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, contractLeft_apply,
   247	      LinearMap.restrictScalars_comp, LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
   248	      Function.comp_apply, AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange_tmul, LinearMap.rTensor_tmul,
   249	      dualBaseChange_tmul, LinearMap.smul_apply, Dual.baseChange_apply_tmul, smul_eq_mul,
   250	      Algebra.mul_smul_comm, mul_one, AlgebraTensorModule.rid_symm_apply]
   251	    rw [← TensorProduct.smul_tmul', ← TensorProduct.tmul_smul, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
   252	  have hbij : Function.Bijective ((contractLeft A P).baseChange B) := by
   253	    rw [hsquare]
   254	    simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe]
   255	    exact (((AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B).symm.bijective.comp
   256	        (Module.Invertible.bijective (R := B) (M := B ⊗[A] P))).comp
   257	        ((Module.Invertible.rTensor_bijective_iff (M := B ⊗[A] P)).mpr
   258	          (bijective_dualBaseChange A B P))).comp
   259	      (AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange A B (Dual A P) P).bijective
   260	  rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor] at hbij
   261	  exact ⟨(Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective A B _).mp hbij⟩

   270	theorem finite_descended [Module.Finite B M] : Module.Finite A D.descended := by
   271	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Finite.equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
   272	  exact Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
   273	
   274	theorem flat_descended [Module.Flat B M] : Module.Flat A D.descended := by
   275	  have : Module.Flat B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv D.descentEquiv
   276	  exact Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct A D.descended B
   277	
   278	theorem finitePresentation_descended [Module.FinitePresentation B M] :
   279	    Module.FinitePresentation A D.descended := by
   280	  have : Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) :=
   281	    Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective D.descentEquiv.symm.toLinearMap
   282	      D.descentEquiv.symm.surjective
   283	      (by simpa using Submodule.fg_bot)
   284	  exact FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B
   285	    D.descended
   286	
   287	theorem projective_descended [Module.Finite B M] [Projective B M] :
   288	    Projective A D.descended := by
   289	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Finite.equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
   290	  have : Projective B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Projective.of_equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
   291	  exact Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B D.descended
   292	
   293	/-- **Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules**: if `M` is an invertible `B`-module
   294	with a descent datum relative to a faithfully flat `A → B`, then the descended `A`-module
   295	is invertible.  Together with `Module.DescentDatum.descentEquiv` (which exhibits

    54	Producing the comparison unit `v` from the piece restriction of `θ` is a gluing step
    55	(the restricted `θ`, twisted by a trivialization of `L` on the affine piece, glues to a
    56	single unit of `Γ(cg⁻¹ V ×_{Spec A} Spec (B ⊗[A] B))` by the `𝒪ˣ`-sheaf axiom, exactly as
    57	the (C1) `witnessBasicSection` construction of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.WitnessCorrection`
    58	does for the trivial-on-cover case); the diagonal and Amitsur hypotheses on `v` are then
    59	the restrictions of `Over.normalizedComparison_diagonal_eq_one` and
    60	`NormalizedCechComparison.coherent`.  The restriction compatibility on overlaps `W ≤ V`
    61	(D2 item 3b) is `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_baseChange`
    62	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.UnitDescentBaseChange`) along `Over.resAlgHomA : Γ(V) →ₐ[A]
    63	Γ(W)`, once the two comparison units are related by base change through
    64	`Over.pieceRingEquiv_naturality`.
    65	-/

    77	/-! ## The descent-cocycle ring identification -/
    78	
    79	/-- **The descent-cocycle ring identification** ((C2) effectivity, brick E2): for an
    80	`A`-algebra `S` (the base-piece ring) and an `A`-algebra `B` (the cover), the ring
    81	`(S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B)` in which a `Module.IsDescentCocycle` over `S → S ⊗[A] B`
    82	lives is the base change to `S` of the whole-cover descent-cocycle ring `B ⊗[A] B`:
    83	`(S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B) ≃ₐ[S] S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)`.  The composite of mathlib's
    84	`cancelBaseChange` (cancelling the middle `S`) and `assoc`. -/
    85	noncomputable def pieceDescentEquiv :
    86	    (S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B) ≃ₐ[S] S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
    87	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange A S S (S ⊗[A] B) B).trans
    88	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.assoc A A S S B B)

    90	@[simp]
    91	lemma pieceDescentEquiv_tmul (s₁ s₂ : S) (b₁ b₂ : B) :
    92	    pieceDescentEquiv A S B ((s₁ ⊗ₜ[A] b₁) ⊗ₜ[S] (s₂ ⊗ₜ[A] b₂))
    93	      = (s₂ * s₁) ⊗ₜ[A] (b₁ ⊗ₜ[A] b₂) := by
    94	  simp only [pieceDescentEquiv, AlgEquiv.trans_apply, cancelBaseChange_tmul,
    95	    TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, Algebra.TensorProduct.assoc_tmul]
    96	
    97	/-- The first coprojection step of `pieceDescentTripleEquiv`, on a pure `S`-tensor:
    98	`congr (refl) pieceDescentEquiv (a ⊗ x) = a ⊗ pieceDescentEquiv x`. -/
    99	private lemma congr_refl_pieceDescentEquiv (a : S ⊗[A] B)
   100	    (x : (S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B)) :
   101	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.congr (AlgEquiv.refl (R := S) (A₁ := S ⊗[A] B))
   102	        (pieceDescentEquiv A S B)) (a ⊗ₜ[S] x)
   103	      = a ⊗ₜ[S] pieceDescentEquiv A S B x := by
   104	  rw [congr_apply, Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul]; rfl

   106	/-- **The triple descent-cocycle ring identification**: the base of the Amitsur cocycle
   107	identity, `(S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] ((S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B)) ≃ₐ[S] S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))`. -/
   108	noncomputable def pieceDescentTripleEquiv :
   109	    (S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] ((S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B))
   110	      ≃ₐ[S] S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)) :=
   111	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.congr (AlgEquiv.refl (R := S) (A₁ := S ⊗[A] B))
   112	      (pieceDescentEquiv A S B)).trans
   113	    ((Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange A S S (S ⊗[A] B) (B ⊗[A] B)).trans
   114	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.assoc A A S S B (B ⊗[A] B)))

   116	@[simp]
   117	lemma pieceDescentTripleEquiv_tmul (s₀ s₁ s₂ : S) (b₀ b₁ b₂ : B) :
   118	    pieceDescentTripleEquiv A S B
   119	        ((s₀ ⊗ₜ[A] b₀) ⊗ₜ[S] ((s₁ ⊗ₜ[A] b₁) ⊗ₜ[S] (s₂ ⊗ₜ[A] b₂)))
   120	      = (s₂ * s₁ * s₀) ⊗ₜ[A] (b₀ ⊗ₜ[A] (b₁ ⊗ₜ[A] b₂)) := by
   121	  rw [pieceDescentTripleEquiv, AlgEquiv.trans_apply, AlgEquiv.trans_apply,
   122	    congr_refl_pieceDescentEquiv, pieceDescentEquiv_tmul, cancelBaseChange_tmul,
   123	    TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, Algebra.TensorProduct.assoc_tmul]

   126	
   127	/-- **`lmul'` compatibility**: the identification intertwines the multiplication of
   128	`M ⊗[S] M` (`M := S ⊗[A] B`) with the base-changed multiplication `id_S ⊗ lmul'` of
   129	`S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)`.  The cochain-level source of the `lmul'_eq_one` normalization. -/
   130	lemma pieceDescentEquiv_lmul' (y : (S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B)) :
   131	    Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' S (S := S ⊗[A] B) y
   132	      = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A)

   140	          Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul'_apply_tmul]
   141	        ring_nf
   142	      | add x y hx hy => simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add, hx, hy]
   143	      | zero => simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_zero, map_zero]
   144	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [TensorProduct.add_tmul, map_add, hx, hy]
   145	    | zero => simp only [TensorProduct.zero_tmul, map_zero]
   146	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
   147	  | zero => simp only [map_zero]

   156	  | tmul m₁ m₂ => induction m₁ with

   158	      | tmul s₂ b₂ =>

   160	          Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def, pieceDescentTripleEquiv_tmul,
   161	          Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, AlgHom.id_apply, Module.descentFace₂₃_apply]
   162	        ring_nf
   163	      | add x y hx hy => simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add, hx, hy]
   164	      | zero => simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_zero, map_zero]
   165	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [TensorProduct.add_tmul, map_add, hx, hy]
   166	    | zero => simp only [TensorProduct.zero_tmul, map_zero]
   167	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
   168	  | zero => simp only [map_zero]

   216	/-! ## The cover-pullback triviality of a descended class
   217	
   218	The image of the Picard class of a descent cocycle under base change to the cover is
   219	trivial: the descended module base-changes back to the cover ring itself. -/
   220	
   221	/-- **The cover-pullback of a descended class is trivial**: for a faithfully flat cover
   222	`R → T`, base change of the Picard class of a descent cocycle back up to `T` is `1`, since
   223	the descended module base-changes to `T` through `Module.DescentDatum.descentEquiv`.  On a
   224	`cg`-saturated affine piece `V` (with `R = Γ(V)`, `T = Γ(V) ⊗[A] B ≅ Γ(cg⁻¹ V)`) this is
   225	the provable half of the D2 item-3a cg-pullback recovery: the descended class `M_V` pulls
   226	back to the trivial class on the cover piece. -/
   227	theorem IsDescentCocycle.mapAlgebra_picClass_eq_one {R T : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing T]
   228	    [Algebra R T] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R T] {u : (T ⊗[R] T)ˣ}
   229	    (hu : Module.IsDescentCocycle u) :
   230	    CommRing.Pic.mapAlgebra R T hu.picClass = 1 := by
   231	  rw [Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass, CommRing.Pic.mapAlgebra_apply,
   232	    CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_one_iff]
   233	  exact ⟨(LinearEquiv.baseChange R T (CommRing.Pic.mk R hu.descended).AsModule hu.descended
   234	      (CommRing.Pic.mk.linearEquiv R hu.descended)).trans
   235	    (Module.DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descentEquiv⟩
   236	
   237	variable (A S B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing S] [CommRing B] [Algebra A S] [Algebra A B]
   238	
   239	/-! ## The per-piece descent unit and its cocycle property -/
   240	
   241	/-- **The per-piece descent unit** ((C2) effectivity, brick E2): the unit of
   242	`(S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B)` corresponding to a comparison unit
   243	`v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ` under the descent-cocycle ring identification
   244	`pieceDescentEquiv`.  On a piece `V`, `v` is the value `Over.pieceEquiv` transports the
   245	piece restriction of the E1 comparison `θ` to. -/
   246	noncomputable def comparisonDescentUnit (v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ) :
   247	    ((S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B))ˣ :=
   248	  Units.map (pieceDescentEquiv A S B).symm.toAlgHom.toRingHom.toMonoidHom v
   249	
   250	@[simp]
   251	lemma pieceDescentEquiv_comparisonDescentUnit_val (v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ) :
   252	    pieceDescentEquiv A S B (comparisonDescentUnit A S B v).val = v.val := by
   253	  change pieceDescentEquiv A S B ((pieceDescentEquiv A S B).symm v.val) = v.val
   254	  exact AlgEquiv.apply_symm_apply _ _
   255	
   256	/-- **The per-piece descent unit of a coherent comparison unit is a descent 1-cocycle**
   257	((C2) effectivity, brick E2).  The diagonal normalization is the `id_S ⊗ lmul'`
   258	hypothesis `hlmul` — the cochain source is `Over.normalizedComparison_diagonal_eq_one`
   259	restricted to the piece; the cocycle identity is the Amitsur identity through the three
   260	cofaces `hcoc` — the cochain source is `NormalizedCechComparison.coherent`.  Both are
   261	transported through the descent-cocycle ring identifications by the coprojection–face
   262	compatibility lemmas. -/
   263	theorem isDescentCocycle_comparisonDescentUnit {v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ}
   264	    (hlmul : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A) v.val
   265	      = 1)
   266	    (hcoc : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₂₃ A B) v.val
   267	          * Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₂ A B) v.val
   268	        = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₃ A B) v.val) :
   269	    Module.IsDescentCocycle (comparisonDescentUnit A S B v) where
   270	  lmul'_eq_one := by
   271	    change Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' S (S := S ⊗[A] B)
   272	      (comparisonDescentUnit A S B v).val = 1
   273	    rw [pieceDescentEquiv_lmul', pieceDescentEquiv_comparisonDescentUnit_val, hlmul]
   274	  cocycle := by
   275	    apply (pieceDescentTripleEquiv A S B).injective
   276	    rw [map_mul, pieceDescentTripleEquiv_descentFace₂₃,
   277	      pieceDescentTripleEquiv_descentFace₁₂, pieceDescentTripleEquiv_descentFace₁₃,
   278	      pieceDescentEquiv_comparisonDescentUnit_val, hcoc]
   279	
   280	/-! ## The descended per-piece Picard class -/
   281	
   282	variable [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
   283	
   284	/-- **The descended per-piece class `M_V`** ((C2) effectivity, brick E2): for a faithfully
   285	flat cover `A → B` and a coherent comparison unit `v`, the Picard class over the base
   286	piece `S = Γ(V)` of the module descended from the per-piece descent cocycle.  Its image
   287	under `CommRing.Pic S → CommRing.Pic (S ⊗[A] B)` is trivial (the descent recovers the
   288	cover-piece ring `M = S ⊗[A] B` twisted by the comparison), so the tracked cg-pullback
   289	recovery of D2 item 3a is the identification of `L` restricted to the piece with the
   290	comparison twist; the restriction compatibility on overlaps (D2 item 3b) is
   291	`Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_baseChange`. -/
   292	noncomputable def comparisonDescentClass {v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ}
   293	    (hlmul : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A) v.val
   294	      = 1)
   295	    (hcoc : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₂₃ A B) v.val
   296	          * Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₂ A B) v.val
   297	        = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₃ A B) v.val) :
   298	    CommRing.Pic S :=
   299	  (isDescentCocycle_comparisonDescentUnit A S B hlmul hcoc).picClass
   300	
   301	/-- **The cg-pullback recovery of the descended per-piece class** (D2 item 3a, provable
   302	half): the descended class `comparisonDescentClass` pulls back to the trivial class on the
   303	cover-piece ring `S ⊗[A] B ≅ Γ(cg⁻¹ V)`.  The full D2 item-3a — that this trivial
   304	cover-pullback *is* the class of `L` restricted to the piece — is the statement that the
   305	comparison unit `v` trivializes `L` on the piece, established when `v` is produced from the
   306	piece restriction of the E1 comparison (the frontier consumed by E3). -/
   307	theorem mapAlgebra_comparisonDescentClass_eq_one {v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ}
   308	    (hlmul : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A) v.val
   309	      = 1)
   310	    (hcoc : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₂₃ A B) v.val
   311	          * Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₂ A B) v.val
   312	        = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₃ A B) v.val) :
   313	    CommRing.Pic.mapAlgebra S (S ⊗[A] B) (comparisonDescentClass A S B hlmul hcoc) = 1 :=
   314	  (isDescentCocycle_comparisonDescentUnit A S B hlmul hcoc).mapAlgebra_picClass_eq_one
   315	
   316	end Module

     9	# The intrinsic theta Cech equalizer over the widened colength algebra
    10	
    11	The intrinsic piece and overlap quotients of `DivisorFamilyAffThetaDescent` are modules over
    12	different local colength algebras. This file restricts all of those actions to the single
    13	widened equalizer algebra `A_D = gluedSubalgebra A`. The two overlap restrictions then become
    14	`A_D`-linear maps, and the intrinsic theta module is their kernel in `A_D`-modules.
    15	
    16	The final declarations give the resulting equalizer its universal property. This is the
    17	module-descent input needed to compare the intrinsic theta line with its piecewise base
    18	changes and descend invertibility, without a `ChartTyping` or any additional hypothesis.
    19	-/

    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    32	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    33	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] [IsProper C.hom]

    40	/-- Restriction of the widened equalizer algebra to one overlap colength algebra. -/
    41	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap (A : AffAdaptation D d) (i j : D.index) :
    42	    ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
    43	  (A.toOvlLeft i j).comp (A.gluedSubalgebraPieceMap i)
    44	
    45	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
    46	/-- The overlap algebra map is independent of whether it is evaluated through the left or
    47	right piece. This is exactly the defining equalizer relation of `A_D`. -/
    48	lemma gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap_eq_right (A : AffAdaptation D d) (i j : D.index) :
    49	    A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap i j =
    50	      (A.toOvlRight i j).comp (A.gluedSubalgebraPieceMap j) := by
    51	  ext c
    52	  change A.toOvlLeft i j (c.1 i) = A.toOvlRight i j (c.1 j)
    53	  exact (A.mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (c : A.chartProd)).mp c.2 (i, j)
    54	
    55	/-- An overlap theta quotient, restricted to an `A_D`-module through the common overlap
    56	algebra map. -/
    57	@[reducible]
    58	noncomputable def thetaOverlapQuotientGluedModule (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    59	    (i j : D.index) :
    60	    Module ↥(gluedSubalgebra A)
    61	      (A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j) :=
    62	  letI : Module (A.ovlColength i j) (A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j) :=
    63	    A.thetaOverlapQuotientModule (π := π) a i j
    64	  Module.compHom (A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j)
    65	    (A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap i j).toRingHom

    68	  thetaOverlapQuotientGluedModule

    70	/-- The intrinsic theta equalizer carries its canonical module structure over the widened
    71	colength algebra outside this construction file as well. -/
    72	@[reducible]
    73	noncomputable instance intrinsicThetaGluedOverModule (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :

   141	    Function.comp_apply, thetaToOverlapLeftGlued,

   153	    A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver_iff]

   157	    (j : D.index) :

   161	
   162	/-- The piece projections from the intrinsic theta equalizer agree on every overlap. -/
   163	theorem intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece_overlap (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
   164	    (i j : D.index) :
   165	    A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ

   167	      A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ

   183	noncomputable def intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift (a : ℕ)
   184	    (f : ∀ j : D.index, M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   185	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j)

   196	    apply Subtype.ext
   197	    funext j
   198	    exact (f j).map_add x y
   199	  map_smul' c x := by
   200	    apply Subtype.ext
   201	    funext j
   202	    exact (f j).map_smul c x

   207	lemma intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift_apply (a : ℕ)
   208	    (f : ∀ j : D.index, M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   209	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j)
   210	    (hf : ∀ i j : D.index,

   212	        A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f j)

   214	    (A.intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift (π := π) a f hf x :

170	/-- The piece-local colength module `Γ(pieces j) ⧸ (f_j)`. -/
   171	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : D.index) : Type u :=
   172	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
   173	
   174	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal, generated by both restricted equations. -/
   175	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : D.index) :
   176	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
   177	  Ideal.span
   178	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
   179	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
   180	
   181	/-- The overlap colength module. -/
   182	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : D.index) : Type u :=
   183	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
   184	
   185	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `i` component. -/
   186	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : D.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   187	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
   188	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
   189	    (by
   190	      intro a ha
   191	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   192	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   193	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   194	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   195	          (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
   196	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   197	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
   198	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   199	
   200	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `j` component. -/
   201	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : D.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   202	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   203	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
   204	    (by
   205	      intro a ha
   206	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   207	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   208	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   209	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   210	          (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
   211	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   212	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
   213	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   214	
   215	/-- The product of the piece-local colengths. -/
   216	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : D.index, A.colength j
   217	
   218	/-- The product of the overlap colengths over ordered index pairs. -/
   219	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : D.index × D.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
   220	
   221	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer. -/
   222	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   223	  LinearMap.pi
   224	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
   225	
   226	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer. -/
   227	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   228	  LinearMap.pi
   229	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   230	
   231	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`**, spelled as a kernel so the `FlatCokernel`
   232	base-change keystone applies verbatim. -/
   233	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   234	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
   235	
   236	/-- The equalizer description of `W(d)`. -/
   237	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   238	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   239	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   240	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   241	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   242	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
   243	
   244	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
   245	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
   246	
   247	/-! ### The certificate -/
   248	
   249	/-- **The colength certificate over a widened cover** — clauses (c1)–(c4) verbatim from
   250	`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`.  Nothing is added and nothing is dropped: the widening
   251	changes where the pieces LIVE, not what the certificate asserts. -/
   252	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
   253	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   254	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
   255	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   256	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
   257	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   258	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
   259	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   260	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
   261	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
   262	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
   263	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
   264	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
   265	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
   266	  flat_coker_diff :
   267	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
   268	
   269	end AffAdaptation
   270	
   271	end AlgebraicGeometry

events.text: A direct precedent exists in the chart-typed carrier: `DivisorFamilyThetaRank.lean` already proves that the theta equalizer is invertible over the glued colength algebra, then derives finite/projective/rank over the base. I’m reading that proof now; if its only chart dependence is the old `IsThetaPaired` packaging, the right move is to port its actual contraction argument to the intrinsic arbitrary-cover equalizer, not invent a new hypothesis or a second descent theory.

    11	/-!
    12	# Invertible modules over a finite algebra: transfer to the base ring (DD-4 (c2)-transport)
    13	
    14	Pure commutative algebra, no schemes (the D1 module-algebra discipline): let `A` be an
    15	`R`-algebra that is finite projective as an `R`-module, and let `M` be an **invertible**
    16	`A`-module (`Module.Invertible`, mathlib's Picard-group vocabulary).  Then `M` is finite
    17	projective over `R` **of the same rank as `A` at every prime**:
    18	
    19	* `Module.Projective.trans` — projectivity descends along a projective algebra: if `A`
    20	  is projective over `R` and `P` projective over `A`, then `P` is projective over `R`
    21	  (the projective mirror of `Module.Projective.of_free_algebra` in
    22	  `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatCokernel`).
    23	* `TensorProduct.baseChangeAlgebraModule` — the base-change collapse
    24	  `(S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M` for an `A`-module `M` (the `A`-algebra structure
    25	  on `S ⊗[R] A` through `Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra`).
    26	* `Module.Invertible.finite_trans` / `Module.Invertible.projective_trans` — the
    27	  finiteness/projectivity transfers.
    28	* `Module.Invertible.rankAtStalk_eq_of_module_finite` — **the rank transfer**: at every
    29	  prime `p` of `R`, `rankAtStalk M p = rankAtStalk A p`.  Route (the semilocal
    30	  Pic-vanishing): the fibre algebra `κ(p) ⊗[R] A` is a finite algebra over the residue
    31	  field, hence artinian, hence semilocal, so its Picard group is trivial (mathlib) and
    32	  the fibre of `M` — an invertible module over the fibre algebra — is **free of rank
    33	  one**; taking `κ(p)`-dimensions gives the claim through `Module.rankAtStalk_eq`.
    34	
    35	The DD-4 consumer instantiates this at `A := ` the glued equalizer algebra of a certified
    36	divisor family (with `Module.Finite`/`Projective`/`rankAtStalk = g` from the certificate
    37	clause (c2)) and `M := ` the Θ-twisted glued module `W(d)^{Θᵃ}`
    38	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyThetaRank`).
    39	-/

    47	/-! ## Projectivity descends along a projective algebra -/
    48	
    49	/-- **Projectivity is transitive**: if `A` is a projective `R`-module and `P` is a
    50	projective `A`-module, then `P` is projective as an `R`-module.  The `A`-splitting
    51	`P →ₗ[A] (P →₀ A)` provided by `Module.projective_def'` restricts to an `R`-splitting,
    52	and `P →₀ A` is a projective `R`-module (a direct sum of copies of `A`, through
    53	`finsuppLequivDFinsupp`). -/
    54	theorem Module.Projective.trans {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (A : Type v) [CommRing A]
    55	    [Algebra R A] {P : Type*} [AddCommMonoid P] [Module A P] [Module R P]
    56	    [IsScalarTower R A P] [Module.Projective R A] [Module.Projective A P] :
    57	    Module.Projective R P := by
    58	  classical
    59	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := Module.projective_def'.mp ‹Module.Projective A P›
    60	  haveI : Module.Projective R (P →₀ A) :=
    61	    Module.Projective.of_equiv (finsuppLequivDFinsupp (R := R) (M := A) (ι := P)).symm
    62	  exact Module.Projective.of_split
    63	    (LinearMap.restrictScalars R s)
    64	    (LinearMap.restrictScalars R (Finsupp.linearCombination A _root_.id))
    65	    (LinearMap.ext fun p => DFunLike.congr_fun hs p)

    67	/-! ## The base-change collapse `(S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M` -/
    68	
    69	namespace TensorProduct
    70	
    71	attribute [local instance] Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    72	
    73	section BaseChangeAlgebraModule
    74	
    75	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    76	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    77	variable (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower R A M]
    78	
    79	/-- The `S`-linear structure map `M →ₗ[R] (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M`, `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`. -/
    80	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit : M →ₗ[R] (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M :=
    81	  LinearMap.restrictScalars R (TensorProduct.mk A (S ⊗[R] A) M 1)
    82	
    83	@[simp]
    84	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit_apply (m : M) :
    85	    baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit S A M m = (1 : S ⊗[R] A) ⊗ₜ[A] m := rfl
    86	
    87	/-- (Implementation) The collapse pairing `(S ⊗[R] A) →ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] S ⊗[R] M`,
    88	`(s ⊗ a, m) ↦ s ⊗ (a • m)`, obtained by currying the composite of the associator with
    89	the `A`-action collapse on the right factor. -/
    90	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing :
    91	    (S ⊗[R] A) →ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] S ⊗[R] M :=
    92	  TensorProduct.curry
    93	    ((LinearMap.lTensor S
    94	        ((LinearMap.liftBaseChange A (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[R] M)).restrictScalars R)) ∘ₗ
    95	      (TensorProduct.assoc R S A M).toLinearMap)
    96	
    97	@[simp]
    98	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul (s : S) (a : A) (m : M) :
    99	    baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M (s ⊗ₜ[R] a) m = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a • m) := by
   100	  simp [baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing]
   101	
   102	/-- The `A`-action on `S ⊗[R] A` through `Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra`, on pure
   103	tensors. -/
   104	lemma rightAlgebra_smul_tmul (a : A) (s : S) (b : A) :
   105	    a • (s ⊗ₜ[R] b) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a * b) := by
   106	  change ((1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] a) * (s ⊗ₜ[R] b) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a * b)
   107	  rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, one_mul]
   108	
   109	/-- (Implementation) The pairing is `A`-balanced. -/
   110	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul (a : A) (x : S ⊗[R] A) (m : M) :
   111	    baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M (a • x) m
   112	      = baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x (a • m) := by
   113	  induction x with
   114	  | zero => simp
   115	  | tmul s b =>
   116	      rw [rightAlgebra_smul_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul,
   117	        baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, mul_smul, smul_comm]
   118	  | add x y hx hy => rw [smul_add, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hx, hy, map_add,
   119	      LinearMap.add_apply]
   120	
   121	/-- (Implementation) The pairing is `S`-semilinear in the first slot. -/
   122	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul_left (c : S) (x : S ⊗[R] A) (m : M) :
   123	    baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M (c • x) m
   124	      = c • baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x m := by
   125	  induction x with
   126	  | zero => simp
   127	  | tmul s b =>
   128	      rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul,
   129	        baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul]
   130	  | add x y hx hy => rw [smul_add, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hx, hy, map_add,
   131	      LinearMap.add_apply, smul_add]
   132	
   133	/-- (Implementation) The additive collapse `(S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M →+ S ⊗[R] M`. -/
   134	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse :
   135	    (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M →+ S ⊗[R] M :=
   136	  TensorProduct.liftAddHom
   137	    { toFun := fun x =>
   138	        { toFun := fun m => baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x m
   139	          map_zero' := by simp
   140	          map_add' := fun m n => by simp }
   141	      map_zero' := by ext m; simp
   142	      map_add' := fun x y => by ext m; simp }
   143	    (fun a x m => baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul S A M a x m)
   144	
   145	@[simp]
   146	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul (x : S ⊗[R] A) (m : M) :
   147	    baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse S A M (x ⊗ₜ[A] m)
   148	      = baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing S A M x m := rfl
   149	
   150	/-- **The base-change collapse**: for an `A`-module `M` and an `R`-algebra `S`, the
   151	base change of `M` along `A → S ⊗[R] A` is the base change along `R → S`,
   152	`S`-linearly: `(S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M` on generators
   153	`(s ⊗ a) ⊗ m ↦ s ⊗ (a • m)`. -/
   154	noncomputable def baseChangeAlgebraModule : (S ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] M where
   155	  toFun := baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse S A M
   156	  map_add' := map_add _
   157	  map_smul' := by
   158	    intro c z
   159	    rw [RingHom.id_apply]
   160	    induction z with
   161	    | zero => simp
   162	    | tmul x m =>
   163	        rw [show c • (x ⊗ₜ[A] m) = (c • x) ⊗ₜ[A] m from TensorProduct.smul_tmul' c x m,
   164	          baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul,
   165	          baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_smul_left]
   166	    | add z w hz hw =>
   167	        rw [smul_add, map_add, map_add, hz, hw, smul_add]
   168	  invFun := LinearMap.liftBaseChange S (baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit S A M)
   169	  left_inv := by
   170	    intro z
   171	    induction z with
   172	    | zero => simp
   173	    | tmul x m =>
   174	        rw [baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul]
   175	        induction x with
   176	        | zero => simp [TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
   177	        | tmul s b =>
   178	            rw [baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul,
   179	              baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit_apply]
   180	            calc s • ((1 : S ⊗[R] A) ⊗ₜ[A] (b • m))
   181	                = s • (b • ((1 : S ⊗[R] A) ⊗ₜ[A] m)) := by
   182	                  rw [TensorProduct.tmul_smul]
   183	              _ = s • ((b • (1 : S ⊗[R] A)) ⊗ₜ[A] m) := by
   184	                  rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul' b _ m]
   185	              _ = (s • b • (1 : S ⊗[R] A)) ⊗ₜ[A] m := TensorProduct.smul_tmul' s _ m
   186	              _ = (s ⊗ₜ[R] b) ⊗ₜ[A] m := by
   187	                  congr 1
   188	                  rw [show b • (1 : S ⊗[R] A) = (1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] (b * 1) from
   189	                    rightAlgebra_smul_tmul S A b 1 1, mul_one, TensorProduct.smul_tmul',
   190	                    smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
   191	        | add x y hx hy =>
   192	            rw [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, map_add, hx, hy, TensorProduct.add_tmul]
   193	    | add z w hz hw =>
   194	        rw [map_add, map_add, hz, hw]
   195	  right_inv := by
   196	    intro z
   197	    induction z with
   198	    | zero => simp
   199	    | tmul s m =>
   200	        rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModuleUnit_apply,
   201	          TensorProduct.smul_tmul' s _ m, baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul,
   202	          show s • (1 : S ⊗[R] A) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : A) by
   203	            rw [show (1 : S ⊗[R] A) = (1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : A) from rfl,
   204	              TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one],
   205	          baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul, one_smul]
   206	    | add z w hz hw => rw [map_add, map_add, hz, hw]
   207	
   208	@[simp]
   209	lemma baseChangeAlgebraModule_tmul_tmul (s : S) (a : A) (m : M) :
   210	    baseChangeAlgebraModule S A M ((s ⊗ₜ[R] a) ⊗ₜ[A] m) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a • m) := by
   211	  change baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse S A M ((s ⊗ₜ[R] a) ⊗ₜ[A] m) = s ⊗ₜ[R] (a • m)
   212	  rw [baseChangeAlgebraModuleCollapse_tmul, baseChangeAlgebraModulePairing_tmul]
   213	
   214	end BaseChangeAlgebraModule
   215	
   216	end TensorProduct

   218	/-! ## The invertible-module transfer -/
   219	
   220	namespace Module.Invertible
   221	
   222	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
   223	
   224	section Transfer
   225	
   226	variable {M : Type u} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower R A M]
   227	
   228	/-- **Finiteness transfer**: an invertible module over a module-finite `R`-algebra is a
   229	finite `R`-module. -/
   230	theorem finite_trans [Module.Finite R A] [Module.Invertible A M] :
   231	    Module.Finite R M :=
   232	  Module.Finite.trans A M
   233	
   234	/-- **Projectivity transfer**: an invertible module over an `R`-algebra that is
   235	projective as an `R`-module is projective over `R`. -/
   236	theorem projective_trans [Module.Projective R A] [Module.Invertible A M] :
   237	    Module.Projective R M :=
   238	  Module.Projective.trans A
   239	
   240	end Transfer

   242	section Rank
   243	
   244	attribute [local instance] Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
   245	
   246	variable {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower R A M]
   247	variable [Module.Finite R A] [Module.Projective R A] [Module.Invertible A M]
   248	
   249	omit [Module.Projective R A] [Module.Invertible A M] in
   250	/-- (Implementation) The fibre algebra `κ(p) ⊗[R] A` of a finite `R`-algebra is
   251	semilocal: it is a finite algebra over the residue field, hence artinian. -/
   252	theorem finite_maximalSpectrum_fiber (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   253	    Finite (MaximalSpectrum (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A)) := by
   254	  haveI : IsArtinianRing (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A) := by
   255	    haveI : IsArtinian p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] A) :=
   256	      isArtinian_of_fg_of_artinian'
   257	    exact isArtinian_of_tower p.asIdeal.ResidueField inferInstance
   258	  infer_instance
   259	
   260	/-- **The rank transfer** (the semilocal Pic-vanishing): an invertible module over a
   261	finite projective `R`-algebra `A` has the same rank as `A` at every prime of `R`.
   262	Route: `rankAtStalk` is the fibre dimension (`Module.rankAtStalk_eq`); the fibre
   263	`κ(p) ⊗[R] M ≃ (κ(p) ⊗[R] A) ⊗[A] M` is an invertible module over the fibre algebra,
   264	which is artinian (hence semilocal), so its Picard group is trivial and the fibre is
   265	free of rank one over the fibre algebra. -/
   266	theorem rankAtStalk_eq_of_module_finite (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   267	    Module.rankAtStalk M p = Module.rankAtStalk A p := by
   268	  haveI : Module.Finite R M := finite_trans (A := A)
   269	  haveI : Module.Projective R M := projective_trans (A := A)
   270	  haveI : Module.Flat R M := Module.Flat.of_projective
   271	  haveI : Module.Flat R A := Module.Flat.of_projective
   272	  rw [Module.rankAtStalk_eq, Module.rankAtStalk_eq]
   273	  set κ := p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   274	  -- the fibre algebra and the fibre of `M` over it
   275	  set Aκ := κ ⊗[R] A with hAκ
   276	  haveI : Finite (MaximalSpectrum Aκ) := finite_maximalSpectrum_fiber (A := A) p
   277	  -- the fibre of `M` as a base change over `A`, an invertible `Aκ`-module
   278	  haveI hinv : Module.Invertible Aκ (Aκ ⊗[A] M) := inferInstance

import AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent
import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.FinitePresentation
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dual.BaseChange
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Finiteness.Descent
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.EquationalCriterion
import Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup
import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.IsBaseChangeHom

/-!
# Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules

Let `A → B` be a faithfully flat map of commutative rings.  This file shows that the
module-theoretic properties *finite*, *finitely presented*, *flat*, *projective* and
*invertible* all descend along `A → B`: if `B ⊗[A] P` has the property over `B`, then `P`
has it over `A`.  Combined with the effectivity theorem of
`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent` this yields: a `B`-module `M` with a descent
datum descends to an `A`-module `M₀` (unique up to canonical isomorphism), and if `M` is
invertible then so is `M₀`.

The descent of invertibility is reduced, via the definition
`Module.Invertible R M ↔ Function.Bijective (contractLeft R M)`, to two ingredients:

* the *dual base-change comparison* `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is an
  isomorphism for `P` finite projective (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`, proved by a
  retract argument from the finite free case, which is `IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight`);
* bijectivity of `A`-linear maps descends along faithfully flat maps
  (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective`).

Finiteness and projectivity of `P` are themselves obtained by descent: mathlib provides
finiteness (`Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`) and flatness
(`Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`); we add finite presentation
(`Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`), and
projectivity follows from flat + finitely presented.

## Main declarations

* `Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`:
  finite presentation descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
* `Module.Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: finite projectivity
  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
* `Module.dualBaseChange A B P : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)`: the dual
  base-change comparison map.
* `Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`: the comparison map is bijective for finite projective
  `P` (over an arbitrary `A`-algebra `B`).
* `Module.Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: invertibility
  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
* `Module.DescentDatum.finite_descended`, `…flat_descended`,
  `…finitePresentation_descended`, `…projective_descended`,
  `…invertible_descended`: for a descent datum on a `B`-module `M` relative to a
  faithfully flat `A → B`, the descended module inherits each property from `M`;
  in particular **an invertible module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
  module**.

All modules live in a single universe `u`.
-/

universe u

open TensorProduct

namespace Module

variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]

/-! ### Descent of finite presentation -/

/-- Finite presentation of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
theorem FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
    [Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
    Module.FinitePresentation A P := by
  have hfin : Module.Finite A P :=
    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
  obtain ⟨n, p, hp⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
  have hpB : Function.Surjective (p.baseChange B) := by
    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    exact LinearMap.lTensor_surjective B hp
  have hker : (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)).FG :=
    Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker (p.baseChange B) hpB
  have hexact := Module.Flat.lTensor_exact B p.exact_subtype_ker_map
  have hinj : Function.Injective ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B) := by
    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    exact Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _
      (LinearMap.ker p).injective_subtype
  have hrange : LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B)
      = LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) := by
    ext x
    rw [LinearMap.mem_range, LinearMap.mem_ker]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩
      simp only [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
      exact hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero y
    · intro hx
      rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor] at hx
      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hexact x).mp hx
      exact ⟨y, by rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]; exact hy⟩
  have e : (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) ≃ₗ[B] LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) :=
    (LinearEquiv.ofInjective _ hinj).trans (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ hrange)
  have : Module.Finite B (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)) := Module.Finite.iff_fg.mpr hker
  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) := Module.Finite.equiv e.symm
  have : Module.Finite A (LinearMap.ker p) :=
    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
  exact Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective p hp (Module.Finite.iff_fg.mp this)

/-- Finite projectivity of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
theorem Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
    [Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] P)] [Projective B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
    Projective A P := by
  have : Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
    Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B (B ⊗[A] P)
  have : Module.FinitePresentation A P :=
    FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B P
  have : Module.Flat A P := Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct A P B
  exact Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation (R := A) (M := P)

/-! ### The dual base-change comparison map -/

section DualBaseChange

variable {A B} in
/-- Two `B`-functionals on `B ⊗[A] X` that agree on the tensors `1 ⊗ₜ x` are equal. -/
private theorem dual_ext {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module A X]
    {F G : Dual B (B ⊗[A] X)} (h : ∀ x : X, F (1 ⊗ₜ x) = G (1 ⊗ₜ x)) : F = G := by
  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro b x
  have hb : b ⊗ₜ[A] x = b • (1 ⊗ₜ[A] x : B ⊗[A] X) := by
    rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, hb, map_smul, h]

variable (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]

/-- The canonical `B`-linear comparison map from the base change of the dual to the dual
of the base change, `b ⊗ₜ f ↦ b • (f.baseChange B)`.  It is bijective for finite
projective `P` (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`). -/
noncomputable def dualBaseChange : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B (Module.Dual.baseChange B)

@[simp] theorem dualBaseChange_tmul (b : B) (f : Dual A P) :
    dualBaseChange A B P (b ⊗ₜ f) = b • Module.Dual.baseChange B f := rfl

/-- Naturality of the dual base-change comparison map. -/
theorem dualBaseChange_naturality {P Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]
    [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q] (g : P →ₗ[A] Q) :
    dualBaseChange A B P ∘ₗ g.dualMap.baseChange B =
      (g.baseChange B).dualMap ∘ₗ dualBaseChange A B Q := by
  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  intro b f
  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply]
  refine dual_ext fun x => ?_
  simp [Module.Dual.baseChange_apply_tmul]

variable {A B} in
private theorem bijective_dualBaseChange_free (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective (dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A)) := by
  have j : IsBaseChange B (TensorProduct.mk A B (Fin n → A) 1) :=
    TensorProduct.isBaseChange A (Fin n → A) B
  have k : IsBaseChange B (Algebra.linearMap A B) := IsBaseChange.linearMap A B
  have hlr : IsBaseChange B (IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom j (Algebra.linearMap A B)) :=
    IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight j k
  have heq : Module.Dual.baseChange (R := A) B (V := Fin n → A)
      = IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom j (Algebra.linearMap A B) := by
    refine LinearMap.ext fun f => dual_ext fun x => ?_
    have h1 := IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom_comp_apply j (Algebra.linearMap A B) f x
    simpa [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one] using h1.symm
  have hlift : dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) = hlr.equiv.toLinearMap := by
    apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
    apply TensorProduct.ext'
    intro b f
    simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, dualBaseChange_tmul,
      IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul, heq]
  rw [hlift]
  exact hlr.equiv.bijective

/-- **The dual commutes with base change for finite projective modules**: the comparison
map `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is bijective when `P` is finite projective. -/
theorem bijective_dualBaseChange [Module.Finite A P] [Projective A P] :
    Function.Bijective (dualBaseChange A B P) := by
  obtain ⟨n, r, hr⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := Module.projective_lifting_property r LinearMap.id hr
  have hfree := bijective_dualBaseChange_free (A := A) (B := B) n
  have hnat_r := dualBaseChange_naturality A B r
  have hnat_s := dualBaseChange_naturality A B s
  -- the two retraction identities
  have hcomp : s.dualMap ∘ₗ r.dualMap = LinearMap.id := by
    ext f x
    simpa using congrArg f (LinearMap.congr_fun hs x)
  have hu : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] Dual A P,
      s.dualMap.baseChange B (r.dualMap.baseChange B x) = x := by
    intro x
    rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hcomp, LinearMap.baseChange_id,
      LinearMap.id_apply]
  have hcompB : (r.baseChange B) ∘ₗ (s.baseChange B) = LinearMap.id := by
    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hs, LinearMap.baseChange_id]
  have hv : ∀ y : Dual B (B ⊗[A] P),
      (s.baseChange B).dualMap ((r.baseChange B).dualMap y) = y := by
    intro y
    rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.dualMap_comp_dualMap, hcompB, LinearMap.dualMap_id,
      LinearMap.id_apply]
  constructor
  · intro x y hxy
    have h1 : dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) (r.dualMap.baseChange B x)
        = dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) (r.dualMap.baseChange B y) := by
      rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, hnat_r, ← LinearMap.comp_apply, hnat_r]
      simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, hxy]
    have h2 := hfree.injective h1
    rw [← hu x, ← hu y, h2]
  · intro y
    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hfree.surjective ((r.baseChange B).dualMap y)
    refine ⟨s.dualMap.baseChange B z, ?_⟩
    have := LinearMap.congr_fun hnat_s z
    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply] at this
    rw [this, hz, hv]

end DualBaseChange

/-! ### Descent of invertibility -/

/-- **Invertibility of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps**: if `A → B` is
faithfully flat and `B ⊗[A] P` is an invertible `B`-module, then `P` is an invertible
`A`-module. -/
theorem Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
    [Module.Invertible B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
    Module.Invertible A P := by
  have hfin : Module.Finite A P :=
    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
  have hproj : Projective A P :=
    Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B P
  -- the contraction square: base change of `contractLeft A P` factors through
  -- `contractLeft B (B ⊗[A] P)` via the dual base-change comparison map
  have hsquare : (contractLeft A P).baseChange B =
      ((AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ contractLeft B (B ⊗[A] P) ∘ₗ
          (dualBaseChange A B P).rTensor (B ⊗[A] P)) ∘ₗ
        (AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange A B (Dual A P) P).toLinearMap := by
    apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
    ext f p
    simp only [AlgebraTensorModule.curry_apply, LinearMap.restrictScalars_self, curry_apply,
      LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, contractLeft_apply,
      LinearMap.restrictScalars_comp, LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
      Function.comp_apply, AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange_tmul, LinearMap.rTensor_tmul,
      dualBaseChange_tmul, LinearMap.smul_apply, Dual.baseChange_apply_tmul, smul_eq_mul,
      Algebra.mul_smul_comm, mul_one, AlgebraTensorModule.rid_symm_apply]
    rw [← TensorProduct.smul_tmul', ← TensorProduct.tmul_smul, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
  have hbij : Function.Bijective ((contractLeft A P).baseChange B) := by
    rw [hsquare]
    simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe]
    exact (((AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B B).symm.bijective.comp
        (Module.Invertible.bijective (R := B) (M := B ⊗[A] P))).comp
        ((Module.Invertible.rTensor_bijective_iff (M := B ⊗[A] P)).mpr
          (bijective_dualBaseChange A B P))).comp
      (AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange A B (Dual A P) P).bijective
  rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor] at hbij
  exact ⟨(Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective A B _).mp hbij⟩

/-! ### Properties of the descended module of a descent datum -/

namespace DescentDatum

variable {A B} {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
variable (D : DescentDatum A B M) [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]

theorem finite_descended [Module.Finite B M] : Module.Finite A D.descended := by
  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Finite.equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
  exact Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B

theorem flat_descended [Module.Flat B M] : Module.Flat A D.descended := by
  have : Module.Flat B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv D.descentEquiv
  exact Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct A D.descended B

theorem finitePresentation_descended [Module.FinitePresentation B M] :
    Module.FinitePresentation A D.descended := by
  have : Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) :=
    Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective D.descentEquiv.symm.toLinearMap
      D.descentEquiv.symm.surjective
      (by simpa using Submodule.fg_bot)
  exact FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B
    D.descended

theorem projective_descended [Module.Finite B M] [Projective B M] :
    Projective A D.descended := by
  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Finite.equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
  have : Projective B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Projective.of_equiv D.descentEquiv.symm
  exact Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B D.descended

/-- **Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules**: if `M` is an invertible `B`-module
with a descent datum relative to a faithfully flat `A → B`, then the descended `A`-module
is invertible.  Together with `Module.DescentDatum.descentEquiv` (which exhibits
`B ⊗[A] M₀ ≃ M`) and `Module.DescentDatum.equivDescended` (uniqueness), this is the
descent theorem for the Picard group. -/
theorem invertible_descended [Module.Invertible B M] : Module.Invertible A D.descended := by
  have : Module.Invertible B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := .congr D.descentEquiv.symm
  exact Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat A B D.descended

end DescentDatum

end Module

    (hc : A.IsCertified g) (a : Nat) (h : D.SwallowedBy d)
    (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
    Module.rankAtStalk (A.IntrinsicThetaGlued (π := pi) a) p = g := by
  obtain ⟨j0, hsub, hmiss⟩ := h
  let e : A.IntrinsicThetaGlued (π := pi) a ≃ₗ[R]
      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0 :=
    (A.intrinsicThetaGluedEquivPieceProdOfSwallowedBy
      (pi := pi) a ⟨j0, hsub, hmiss⟩).trans
        (A.thetaPieceProdEquivSwallowingPiece (pi := pi) a hmiss)
  have hpiece : Module.rankAtStalk
      (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0) p =
      Module.rankAtStalk (A.colength j0) p := by
    letI : Module.Finite R (A.colength j0) := hc.finite_colength j0
    letI : Module.Projective R (A.colength j0) := hc.projective_colength j0
    letI : IsScalarTower R (A.colength j0)
        (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0) :=
      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl
    letI : Module.Invertible (A.colength j0)
        (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0) :=
      A.invertible_thetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0
    exact Module.Invertible.rankAtStalk_eq_of_module_finite p
  have hcolength : Module.rankAtStalk (A.colength j0) p = g := by
    let ecol : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.colength j0 :=
      (A.gluedEquivChartProd_of_swallowedBy ⟨j0, hsub, hmiss⟩).trans
        (A.chartProdEquivSwallowingPiece hmiss)
    calc
      Module.rankAtStalk (A.colength j0) p = Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p :=
        (congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv ecol) p).symm
      _ = g := hc.rankAtStalk_glued p
  calc
    Module.rankAtStalk (A.IntrinsicThetaGlued (π := pi) a) p =
        Module.rankAtStalk (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0) p :=
      congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv e) p
    _ = Module.rankAtStalk (A.colength j0) p := hpiece
    _ = g := hcolength

section WindowQuotientTransport

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsDominant pi] [IsIntegral C.left]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]

/-- The swallowed descent supplies the projective window-quotient input used by the
frame-cover layer. The quotient is identified with the intrinsic theta carrier by the
cover-independent equivalence, so no chart typing is reintroduced here. -/
theorem IsCertified.projective_intrinsicWindowQuotient_of_swallowedBy
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (hc : A.IsCertified g) (a : Nat)
    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k pi
      (relThetaCocycle C k pi a)).H1)
    (hMa : windowM_choice pi hpi g ≤ a) (h : D.SwallowedBy d) :
    Module.Projective R ((R ⊗[k]
      ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)) ⧸
        divisorWindow d ha1) := by
  letI : Module.Projective R (A.IntrinsicThetaGlued (π := pi) a) :=
    IsCertified.projective_intrinsicThetaGlued_of_swallowedBy (pi := pi) hc a h
  exact Module.Projective.of_equiv
    (AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.IsCertified.intrinsicWindowQuotEquiv
      C R pi hc hpi hO hchi ha1 hMa).symm

/-- Finite companion for the same direct window-quotient route. -/
theorem IsCertified.finite_intrinsicWindowQuotient_of_swallowedBy
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (hc : A.IsCertified g) (a : Nat)
    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k pi
      (relThetaCocycle C k pi a)).H1)
    (hMa : windowM_choice pi hpi g ≤ a) (h : D.SwallowedBy d) :
    Module.Finite R ((R ⊗[k]
      ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)) ⧸
        divisorWindow d ha1) := by
  letI : Module.Finite R (A.IntrinsicThetaGlued (π := pi) a) :=
    IsCertified.finite_intrinsicThetaGlued_of_swallowedBy (pi := pi) hc a h
  exact Module.Finite.equiv
    (AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.IsCertified.intrinsicWindowQuotEquiv
      C R pi hc hpi hO hchi ha1 hMa).symm

/-- Constant-rank companion for the frame-cover input. -/
theorem IsCertified.rankAtStalk_intrinsicWindowQuotient_of_swallowedBy
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (hc : A.IsCertified g) (a : Nat)
    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k pi
      (relThetaCocycle C k pi a)).H1)
    (hMa : windowM_choice pi hpi g ≤ a) (h : D.SwallowedBy d)
    (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
    Module.rankAtStalk ((R ⊗[k]
      ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)) ⧸
        divisorWindow d ha1) p = g := by
  rw [congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv
    (AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.IsCertified.intrinsicWindowQuotEquiv
      C R pi hc hpi hO hchi ha1 hMa)) p]
  exact hc.rankAtStalk_intrinsicThetaGlued_of_swallowedBy a h p

end WindowQuotientTransport
